caseno: Appeal from Original Decree No. 281 of 1991.
lawyer:
ABM Khairul Haque with Mrs. Snigdha Haque, Advocates ----- For the Appellant.
Nurul Islam Chowdhury with Md. Omar Farook, Advocates -----For the Respondent No.4.
parties:
Sonali Bank ----- Appellant
Vs
Hare Krishna Das & others ----- Respondents
full_judgment: The defendant Nos. 1-3 did not contest the suit. The defendant No. 4 filed written statement contending, inter alia, that the suit is not maintainable and there is no cause of action for the suit. The suit is false and fabricated. That the suit is bad for non-joinder of parties.That this defendant is not a necessary party. Since this defendant is admittedly a guarantor he has no liability to pay the debt of the borrower. The plaintiff Bank must realise the entire amount of loan with interest from the borrower by attaching the personal properties of the borrower and after doing all these if there remains any amount to be paid to the Bank then and then only the guarantor will be followed up to pay the said unrecovered amount. This defendant did not sign any balance confirmation certificate nor did he create any equitable mortgage in favour of the plaintiff Bank. The defendant No. 1 in collusion with the plaintiff obtained some signatures of the defendant on some blank papers. This defendant is not aware of any tripartite agreement which might have been created with those signed blank papers. The further case of this defendant is that he did neither create any promissory note nor he has signed any other documents as alleged by the plaintiff. He did not take the loan and, as such, he is not liable to pay the claimed amount. The plaintiff cannot get any relief in the suit and there cannot be any direction upon this defendant to pay the decretal amount unless the decretal amount, if any, is first of all recovered from the other defendants who were allowed to take the loan. There cannot be any personal decree against this defendant, so the suit must fail.
